policy_note: The selected HaGeZi source is Pro Mini. HaGeZi describes the Pro tier as Balanced with low-to-moderate breakage risk; this project therefore treats it as a review-focus source, not as an author-defined strict/aggressive tier. Comparison memberships are descriptive only and are not independent votes. OISD Small and Big are included as comparison-only sources because the user's source-philosophy concern explicitly includes OISD; they remain candidate-only and are not production inputs. Their presence is a comparison, not an independent vote. Active production-source explicit allow rules are global compatibility vetoes over conflicting production-source blocks; this favors low false-positive risk over maximum blocking. Candidate-only source allows are audit signals only and never alter production output.

lineage_evidence.interpretation: The HaGeZi source catalogue lists these as build inputs; this does not mean every listed rule is copied into Pro Mini.
The 1Hosts contributor/input catalogue contains these upstream URLs; the catalogue alone does not prove each entry survives into the Lite output.

policy_profiles.philosophy: Balanced coverage with low-to-moderate breakage risk. Mini is a size-optimized version of Pro, not a more aggressive tier. Do not label this selected input as HaGeZi Ultimate or strict.

sources: OISD Blocklist Small (AdGuard Registry candidate only)
OISD Blocklist Big (AdGuard Registry benchmark only; higher FP risk)
policy_profiles.philosophy: The maintainer explicitly prioritizes a functional internet experience and describes zero breakage as the goal; legitimate shared-use domains may be omitted when blocking them would break legitimate content. Candidate-only comparison; never auto-promote.

Published filtering policy requires sufficient site traffic for site-specific rules and documents exceptions and limitations, including contextual advertising and paywall-related behavior. Absence from the list is not an explicit allow.

conflict_resolution.rationale: An explicit allow published by an active production DNS/Hosts maintainer is treated as a compatibility exception across the merged output. It overrides overlapping block rules from other active production sources. This intentionally favors avoiding false positives over maximum ad/tracker coverage.
conflict_resolution.audit_requirement: Every active production-source allow that overlaps a compiled block must remain effective in the compiled Full output; any missing effective allow is a hard build failure.
conflict_resolution.project_whitelist: Project-maintained whitelist remains an additional global compatibility exception.
conflict_resolution.non_claim: This policy does not treat source absence as an allow decision and does not claim upstream source independence.
